#**Overview**

This document presents the data analysis for Study 1, and replicates this analysis both using the full sample with no exclusions (pg 12), and excluding anyone who expressed an initially neutral attitude about UBI (pg 18).

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(comment=NA, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, echo=FALSE)
library(dplyr)
library(psych)
library(knitr)
library(tidyr)
library(broom)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
library(gridExtra)
#library(qdap)
library(Rmisc)
library(lsr)
```


#Data Cleaning

We begin with the full dataset of 1180 people who completed the survey, then remove everyone who failed the attention check, or who were excluded based on an independent coder's judgement of whether they (1) generated an argument and (2) the argument was for the appropriate side

```{r}
d_full <- read.csv("Study 1 data preexclusions.csv")
d_full$condition <- factor(d_full$condition, levels = c("argument", "opposition argument"), labels = c("Control", "Perspective Taking"))

d <- d_full %>%
  filter(attcheck == 1) %>%
  filter(exclude != "Y") 
```

Consistent with our preregistration plan, we excluded 182 (15.4%) who failed the attention check, completed the survey multiple times, or did not follow instructions, leaving a sample of 998 participants (79.7% female, Mage = 44.05).

#Descriptive Statistics

##Participant gender

1 indicates female, 2 indicates male, 3 indicates other

```{r}
table(d$dem.gender)
```

##Participant Age

Mean and CI age:
```{r}
CI(d$dem.age, ci=0.95)
```

\newpage

#Initial Attitude

We begin by comparing the initial distribution of attitudes by condition, to confirm random assignment.
```{r}
d_PT <- filter(d, condition == "Perspective Taking")
d_control <- filter(d, condition == "Control")
t.test(d_PT$Q1.att_1, d_control$Q1.att_1)
```

Cohen's D:
```{r}
cohensD(d_PT$Q1.att_1, d_control$Q1.att_1)
```

Control:
```{r}
CI(d_control$Q1.att_1)
```

Perspective Taking:
```{r}
CI(d_PT$Q1.att_1)
```

Initial attitudes did not differ between the control (M = 54.02, 95% CI [50.96, 57.07]) and perspective-taking (M = 53.77, 95% CI [50.68, 56.85]) conditions, t(996) = -0.11, p = .91.

#Midpoint

How many people indicated the midpoint?
```{r}
d_50 <- filter(d, Q1.att_1 == 50)
nrow(d_50)

d_noneutral <- filter(d, Q1.att_1 != 50)
```

Participants who indicated a neutral attitude (exactly the midpoint; N = 84) were randomly assigned to a side. All significant relationships reported remain significant when these participants are excluded (see pg 18).

\newpage

#Receptiveness

Receptiveness is measured by 4 items, specifically:

- How receptive do you feel toward the specific argument that you wrote about?

- How open-minded do you feel toward the specific argument that you wrote about? 

- How receptive do you feel toward the perspective (in favor of /against UBI) in general?

- How open-minded do you feel toward the perspective (in favor of/against UBI) in general?

##Creating an index for receptiveness

We begin by computing the alpha for receptiveness:

```{r}
receptiveness <- dplyr::select(d, Q3.receparg, Q4.openarg, Q5.recepgen, Q6.opengen)
alphaRecep <- psych::alpha(receptiveness)
kable(alphaRecep$total)
```

Because our alpha is acceptable (alpha = 0.85), we then combine the 4 receptiveness items into a single index.
```{r}
d$receptiveness <- (d$Q3.receparg + d$Q4.openarg + d$Q5.recepgen + d$Q6.opengen)/4
```


\newpage

#Effect of condition on receptiveness

To explore the effect of condition on receptiveness, we employ an unpaired samples t-test, assuming approximately equal variances 

```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
perspective <- filter(d, condition == "Perspective Taking")
control <- filter(d, condition == "Control")
t.test(perspective$receptiveness, control$receptiveness, paired=FALSE, var.equal=TRUE)
```

Cohen's D:
```{r}
cohensD(perspective$receptiveness, control$receptiveness)
```

Control:
```{r}
CI(control$receptiveness, ci = 0.95)
```
Perspective Taking:
```{r}
CI(perspective$receptiveness, ci = 0.95)
```

Participants reported less receptiveness to the counterattitudinal view in the perspective-taking (M = 3.78, 95% CI [3.65, 3.91]) relative to control (M = 4.10, 95% CI [3.98, 4.22]) condition, t(996)=-3.59, p < .001. 

#Graph

```{r}
se_plus <- function(x) mean(x) + sqrt(var(x)/length(x))
se_minus <- function(x) mean(x) - sqrt(var(x)/length(x))

limits <- aes(ymax = se_u, ymin= se_l)
dodge <- position_dodge(width=0.9)

summary <- d %>% 
  dplyr::group_by(condition) %>% 
  dplyr::summarise("Receptiveness" = mean(receptiveness, na.rm=TRUE), "se_u"=se_plus(receptiveness), "se_l"=se_minus(receptiveness)) 

p1 <- ggplot(data=summary, aes(x=condition, y=Receptiveness, fill=condition)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") + 
  geom_errorbar(limits, position=dodge, width=0.25) + 
  labs(x="Condition", y="Receptiveness") +
  guides(fill=FALSE) +
  theme_hc() + 
  theme(text=element_text(family="Calibri", size=14)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#ffad99", "#05C68A", "#17699E"))

# Colors (SPSP theme)
# peach: #ffad99
# green: #05C68A
# blue: #17699E

#p1
#ggsave("Study_1_Receptiveness.png", scale=1, width=100, height=100, units="mm", dpi=1000)
```

\newpage

#Attitude Change

We calculate attitude change toward the counterattitudinal position for all participants, such that positive numbers always indicate movement in the counterattitudinal direction, while negative numbers indicate movement in the proattitudinal direction.

```{r}
d$att.change <- ifelse(d$side == "against", d$Q1.att_1 - d$Q2.attT2_1, NA)

d$att.change <- ifelse(d$side == "in favor of", d$Q2.attT2_1 - d$Q1.att_1, d$att.change)
```

#Effect of Condition on Attitude Change

```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
perspective <- filter(d, condition == "Perspective Taking")
control <- filter(d, condition == "Control")
t.test(perspective$att.change,
       control$att.change,
       paired=FALSE, var.equal=TRUE)
```

Cohen's D:
```{r}
cohensD(perspective$att.change, control$att.change)
```

Control:
```{r}
CI(control$att.change, ci=0.95)
```
Perspective Taking:
```{r}
CI(perspective$att.change, ci=0.95)
```

Participants showed less change toward the counterattitudinal view in the perspective-taking (M = 5.06, SD = 14.10) relative to control (M = 8.29, SD = 18.12) condition, t(996)=-3.15, p = .002.

#Value/Moral Congruence

Value/Moral Congruence is measured by 3 items, specifically:

- To what extent is this argument congruent with your own values?

- To what extent does this argument fit with your worldview?

- To what extent does this argument reflect your own personal morals?

## Creating an index for value congruence

We begin by computing the alpha for value congruence

```{r, echo=FALSE}
valuecongruence <- dplyr::select(d, Q7.congruent, Q8.fitworldview, Q9.morals)
alphaCongruence <- psych::alpha(valuecongruence)
kable(alphaCongruence$total)
```

Because alpha is satisfactory (alpha = 0.92), we create a single index for value congruence. I've also recoded it so that higher means more congruent. 

```{r}
d$congruence <- 8 - (d$Q7.congruent + d$Q8.fitworldview + d$Q9.morals)/3
```

\newpage

##Effect of condition on value congruence

To explore the effect of condition on receptiveness, we employ anunpaired samples t-test, assuming approximately equal variances


```{r, fig.margin=TRUE}
perspective <- filter(d, condition == "Perspective Taking")
control <- filter(d, condition == "Control")
t.test(perspective$congruence,
       control$congruence,
       paired=FALSE, var.equal=TRUE)
```

Cohen's D:
```{r}
cohensD(perspective$congruence, control$congruence)
```

Perspective:
```{r}
CI(perspective$congruence, ci=.95)
```
Control:
```{r}
CI(control$congruence, ci = .95)
```

Participants reported less value-congruent arguments in the perspective-taking (M = 3.64, SD = 1.80) relative to control (M = 4.23, SD = 1.80) condition, t(996)=-5.17, p < .001. 


\newpage

# Mediation 1: Condition -> Congruence -> Receptiveness

In this mediation model, we test the account where value congruence mediates the effect of condition on receptiveness, using the R package *mediation*

```{r, message=FALSE, comment=NA, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
library(mediation)
d$recep_s <- scale(d$receptiveness)
d$att.change_s <- scale(d$att.change)
d$congruence_s <- as.numeric(scale(d$congruence))

modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ condition, data=d)
kable(tidy(modelm))

modely <- lm(recep_s ~ condition + congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely))

modely1 <- lm(recep_s ~ congruence_s, data = d)
kable(tidy(modely1))

med_model2 <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely, treat="condition",
                                sims=500,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s")

summary(med_model2)
```

Condition affected value-congruence (beta = -.32, t(996) = -5.17, p < .001) and value-congruence predicted receptiveness (beta = .43, t(996) = 15.01, p < .001). As hypothesized, the indirect effect of condition on receptiveness was significant (ab = -.14, 95% CI = -.19 to -.08). 


# Mediation 2: Condition -> Congruence -> Attitude Change

In this mediation model, we test the account where value congruence mediates the effect of condition on attitude change, using the R package *mediation*

```{r, message=FALSE, comment=NA, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
d$recep_s <- scale(d$receptiveness)
d$att.change_s <- scale(d$att.change)
d$congruence_s <- as.numeric(scale(d$congruence))

modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ condition, data=d)
kable(tidy(modelm))

modely <- lm(att.change_s ~ condition + congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely))

modely1 <- lm(att.change_s ~ congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely1))

med_model1 <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely,
                                treat="condition",
                                sims = 5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s",
                   control.value = "Control",
                   treat.value="Perspective Taking")

summary(med_model1)
```

Condition affected value-congruence (beta = -.32, t(996) = -5.17, p < .001) and value-congruence predicted attitude change (beta = .18, t(996)=5.70, p < .001). As hypothesized, the indirect effect of condition on attitude change through value-congruence was significant attitude change: ab = -.05, 95% CI = -.09 to -.03). 


\newpage

#**Analysis on full sample**

This section replicates the above findings with the full sample.

```{r}
d <- d_full
```

#Receptiveness

##Computing alpha and index creation
```{r}
receptiveness <- dplyr::select(d, Q3.receparg, Q4.openarg, Q5.recepgen, Q6.opengen)
alphaRecep <- psych::alpha(receptiveness)
kable(alphaRecep$total)

d$receptiveness <- (d$Q3.receparg + d$Q4.openarg + d$Q5.recepgen + d$Q6.opengen)/4
```

##Effect of condition on receptiveness
```{r}
perspective <- filter(d, condition == "Perspective Taking")
control <- filter(d, condition == "Control")
t.test(perspective$receptiveness, control$receptiveness, paired=FALSE, var.equal=TRUE)
```


Participants reported less receptiveness to the counterattitudinal view in the perspective-taking (M = 3.80, SD = 1.45) relative to control (M = 4.09, SD = 1.40) condition, t(1178)=-3.53, p < .001.

## Mediation 1: Condition -> Congruence -> Receptiveness

```{r, message=FALSE, comment=NA, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
d$recep_s <- scale(d$receptiveness)
d$att.change_s <- scale(d$att.change)
d$congruence_s <- as.numeric(scale(d$congruence))

modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ condition, data=d)

kable(tidy(modely))

modely1 <- lm(recep_s ~ congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely1))

med_model2 <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely, treat="condition",
                                sims=5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s")

summary(med_model2)
```

Condition affected value-congruence (beta = -.30, t(1178) = -5.14, p < .001) and value-congruence predicted receptiveness (beta = .36, t(1178) = 13.22, p < .001). As hypothesized, the indirect effect of condition on receptiveness was significant (ab = -.10, 95% CI = -.15 to -.06).

```{r, message=FALSE, comment=NA, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
d$recep_s <- scale(d$receptiveness)
d$att.change_s <- scale(d$att.change)
d$congruence_s <- as.numeric(scale(d$congruence))

modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ condition, data=d)
kable(tidy(modelm))

modely <- lm(att.change_s ~ condition + congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely))

modely1 <- lm(att.change_s ~ congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely1))

med_model1 <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely,
                                treat="condition",
                                sims = 5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s",
                   control.value = "Control",
                   treat.value="Perspective Taking")

summary(med_model1)
```

Condition affected value-congruence (beta = -.33, t(912) = -4.99, p < .001) and value-congruence predicted receptiveness (beta = .19, t(912) = 5.81, p < .001). As hypothesized, the indirect effect of condition on receptiveness was significant (ab = -.06, 95% CI = -.09 to -.03). 

## Mediation 2: Condition -> Congruence -> Receptiveness

```{r, message=FALSE, comment=NA, warning=FALSE, cache=TRUE}
modelm <- lm(congruence_s ~ condition, data=d)
kable(tidy(modelm))

modely <- lm(recep_s ~ condition + congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely))

modely1 <- lm(recep_s ~ congruence_s, data=d)
kable(tidy(modely1))

med_model2 <- mediation::mediate(modelm, modely, treat="condition",
                                sims=5000,
                                boot=TRUE,
                   mediator="congruence_s")

summary(med_model2)
```

Condition affected value-congruence (beta = -.33, t(912) = -4.99, p < .001) and value-congruence predicted receptiveness (beta = .44, t(912) = 14.78, p < .001). As hypothesized, the indirect effect of condition on receptiveness was significant (ab = -.14, 95% CI = -.20 to -.08).
